verdict.rationale: Nix's own CLI resolves and installs project dependencies without prompts: `nix-shell` builds or downloads declared dependencies, `nix-shell --run` executes a command in that environment, and `nix-env --upgrade` updates packages. Nothing in the pack documents exit-code semantics or machine-readable errors, and one hands-on user reports having to 'dig deep to fix errors'. missing for 10: documented exit codes, structured or clear error output, explicit non-interactive/CI flags for dependency updates, independent corroboration of agent-driven use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent install and update project dependencies non-interactively, with clear exit codes and errors when something fails

citations.quote: the command `nix-shell` will build or download those dependencies if they’re not already in your Nix store
you can do `nix-shell --run "<some command>"`, and it will make sure you have all of the correct dependencies.
